  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

  The project is a request by the Planning Commission to review the existing conditions
  and on-going operations of a bail bond and check cashing facility known as Pro Club
  Store located at 1475-C East Palmdale Boulevard. The purpose of the review is to
  determine the level of compliance with the Conditions of Approval, determine if the
  business is operating in an appropriate manner and determine whether sufficient
  evidence exists regarding non-compliance and on-going operation to warrant modification
  or revocation of the CUP.

  BACKGROUND

  On February 8, 2018, the Planning Commission approved CUP 17-016 through
  RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-005. The approval included establishment of a bail bond
  and check cashing facility within an existing 400 square foot tenant space located at
  1475-C East Palmdale Boulevard. The facility included a customer waiting area, an office
  space and was intended to provide security bail bond and check cashing services.

  On July 8, 2021, the Planning Commission reviewed a request for direction from staff with
  respect to the operation of the business. The memorandum provided to the Planning
  Commission included an incident crime report from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department dated March 9, 2021, regarding crime at the location. Based on the
  information provided at this meeting, the Planning Commission directed staff to initiate a
  full investigation of CUP 17-016 pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section
  17.22.060.

  ANALYSIS

  Upon request from the Planning Commission to initiate a full investigation into the Pro
  Club Store located at 1475-C East Palmdale Boulevard, staff has compiled Code
  Enforcement cases, incident crime reports from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department and has utilized the information to provide an analysis of the violation of
  several Conditions of Approval.

  Staff has determined that the business is a source of crime and is a nuisance to other
  properties in the vicinity. The business is not beneficial and desirous to the community
  and will not be beneficial and desirous to the community even with strict adherence to the
  Conditions of Approval. The evidence indicates that the establishment, and the business
  owner, are associated with narcotics, gambling, and other criminal activity.

Code Enforcement

After approval of CUP 17-016 by the Planning Commission on February 8, 2018, a
complaint was filed on December 17, 2018 (CE18-04709) with the Code Enforcement
Division regarding activity at the business location. The complainant believed illegal
gambling was occurring at the location mainly between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 3:00
a.m. and stated that people were urinating outside and around the building. The
complainant also stated that smoking marijuana and drinking in the parking lot was a daily
occurrence. A Code Enforcement officer visited the location, but could not confirm the
allegations, and the case was closed.

On February 27, 2020, Code Enforcement inspected the Pro Club Store and found drug
paraphernalia for sale, which included pipes used for smoking tobacco, marijuana, and
methamphetamine. The business was also selling tobacco without a license. The store
owner did not have a license to sell tobacco at the time and the Code Enforcement Officer
advised the owner to obtain a tobacco license from the City and cited the owner for the
drug paraphernalia (CE20-00655). A tobacco license was never obtained, but the case
was closed during a follow up inspection on March 25, 2021.

On May 5, 2021, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Departments, Partners Against Crime
team filed a Code Enforcement Case (CE21-01225) for illegal gambling following the legal
search of the property on April 28, 2021, through a search warrant, as discussed below.

Criminal Activity

Staff has received several incident crime reports from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department that detail illegal activity within the Pro Club Store at 1475-C East Palmdale
Boulevard and within the parking lot.

The Pro Club Store owner has been arrested multiple times for illegal activity taking place
within this business location. Specifically, illegal gambling machines have been seized
on  two  separate  occasions,  on  March  19,  2019,  and
April 28, 2021 (ATTACHMENTS 2 and 5). On both occasions, an investigation was
conducted at 1475-C East Palmdale Boulevard following complaints regarding illegal
gambling and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Deputies seized illegal gambling
machines.

On April 22, 2019, Deputies were patrolling the area of 15 th Street East when they
observed a man leaning against a signpost, struggling to maintain his balance outside of

  1475-C East Palmdale Boulevard (ATTACHMENT 3). As Deputies entered into the
  parking lot, Mr. Hawatmeh walked out of the Pro Club Store toward the man outside with
  an outreached hand as if he was going to hand something to him. Mr. Hawatmeh then
  noticed the patrol vehicle, appeared nervous and walked back into the business.
  Deputies detained the man outside. Mr. Hawatmeh then walked out of the business and
  identified himself as the business owner. Both Mr. Hawatmeh and the other individual
  were detained pending a narcotics investigation. After conducting field tests, both
  individuals were determined to be under the influence of a controlled substance and
  arrested. After being arrested, Mr. Hawatmeh was searched, and a baggie of suspected
  methamphetamine was found in his interior jacket pocket.

  On March 9, 2021, Deputies entered into the parking lot of 1475 East Palmdale Boulevard
  around 4:00 a.m. (ATTACHMENT 4). As they entered the parking lot, they observed two
  men who appeared nervous abruptly walked into the Pro Club Store (1475-C East
  Palmdale Boulevard). Due to the time of night and the fact that the surrounding
  businesses were closed at the time, Deputies approached the Pro Club Store to further
  investigate. The door of the store was locked but was immediately opened by the store
  owner, Mr. Hawatmeh, who allowed Deputies to enter. Upon entering, Deputies observed
  eight patrons utilizing three video gambling machines, also referred to as “tap tap”
  machines. Mr. Hawatmeh gave consent for deputies to search the premises and also
  informed the deputies that he had a firearm behind the counter in a pink bag. Deputies
  went to secure the firearm that was behind the counter. During this time, Mr. Hawatmeh
  retrieved a black mesh bag from behind the counter and placed it in a refrigerator. When
  deputies asked if there were drugs in the bag, Mr. Hawatmeh indicated “drugs, I don’t
  know”. A search of the bag revealed a substance that resembled methamphetamine.
  Deputies reviewed surveillance footage at the counter which showed Mr. Hawatmeh
  holding a bag of suspected methamphetamine and handing suspected
  methamphetamine to several persons in exchange for cash.  Concluding the
  investigation, Deputies seized a revolver, a plastic bag containing a large amount of
  methamphetamine as well as several smaller baggies, large quantities of marijuana,
  ecstasy pills, several live ammunition rounds, digital scales and $649 in cash. The Pro
  Club Store owner was arrested for possession of a firearm with the intent to commit a
  felony, possession of narcotics with a firearm, possession of controlled substances for
  sale and operating or minting a drug house. The Deputies then spoke with the first two
  men observed walking into the location as well as each of the patrons that were inside at
  the time of the investigation. All of the patrons claimed they were unaware of any
  weapons or drugs within the location and four patrons admitted to playing the “tap tap”
  machines, but stated they were unaware it was illegal.

On April 28, 2021, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department served a search warrant
at 1475-C East Palmdale Boulevard (ATTACHMENT 5). Upon entering, the business
owner was observed behind the counter and several patrons were observed around three
“tap tap” machines. The business owner and all patrons were detained while officers
searched the premise. While searching the premise, officers found a bag of
methamphetamine, hundreds of small plastic baggies, xanax pills, numerous glass stems
with methamphetamine burned onto them, a notebook that appeared to contain pay and
owe sheets and $275 in cash. Upon concluding the investigation, it was determined that
the business owner was operating or minting a drug house, and he was arrested for
possession of methanphetamine for sale, as well as charged with operating an illegal
casino. The drugs, paraphernalia, currency and gambling machines were all seized. In
addition, three patrons admitted to gambling at the location on several occasions and
were arrested. A fourth patron was arrested for possession of drug paraphernalia.

In addition to the crimes directly associated with the business, there are also numerous
reports detailing arrests made within the parking area of 1475 East Palmdale Boulevard.
Two include drug deals; one involving Deputies performing a patrol check at the location
and arresting an individual for possession of narcotics (ATTACHMENT 6); another
involved an informant calling about an individual suspected of selling drugs
(ATTACHMENT 7). Upon investigation by a Deputy, an individual was arrested for
possession of a controlled substance. While these incident reports detail crimes
committed in the parking lot at 1475 East Palmdale Boulevard and are not directly
associated with the Pro Club Store, the crimes are indicative of the business operations
at the Pro Club Store.

Legal Action

In light of the search warrant and multiple arrests made at 1475 East Palmdale Boulevard,
the City has filed a complaint (ATTACHMENT 8) against the property owner (Jordann &
Co. LLC) of the shopping center, as well as the business owner for the Pro Club Store
(Raed and Sons Inc.), to abate the nuisance of the property for drugs and gambling.

Condition of Approval Compliance

The Pro Club Store is in violation of several of the Conditions of Approval within
RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-005 and the PMC and is not being operated in an
appropriate manner. The business practices and operations are detrimental to public
health, safety and welfare as described below.

  Condition No. 16 of RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-005 states:

  A business license shall be obtained from the Business License Divison.

  As of October 7, 2021, a business license for a bail bond and check cashing has not been
  obtained by the Pro Club Store owner. The Pro Club Store has had a business license
  for general merchandise retail since December 7, 2017.

  Condition No. 17 of RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-005 states:

  The applicant shall provide the Crime Prevention Division with a security plan. This
  plan should detail systems that the tenant intends on installing to protect patrons,
  visitors, employees, and company property/assets on site. The plan shall address
  issues such as safes to be installed, alarm systems, deployment of any security
  personnel, funds transportation measures, hours of operation, shift personnel
  staffing, CCTV applications, type of loss prevention/crime prevention training
  provided to employees, etc. Additional conditions of approval may be added if plan
  is found to be insufficient.

  As of October 7, 2021, the applicant has not submited a security plan to the Crime
  Prevention Division detailing security systems installed to protect patrons, visitors,
  employees and company property/assets on site.

  Condition No. 18 of RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-005 states:

  The bail bond and check cashing use shall be limited to the hours of operation
  Monday through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to
  4:00 p.m., and closed Sunday.

  The business has been observed to be open outside of the hours of operation on multiple
  occasions based on the attached Incident Reports from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department.

  Condition No. 19 of RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-005 states:

  The operation of the business shall comply fully with all the rules and regulations
  of the PMC.

The business is in violation of the PMC in regard to public nuisance. Pursuant to PMC
Section 8.10.020(M), the buisness is considered a public nuisance due to the repetative
illegal activities that occur at the business including drug activity, gambling and public
uriniaition.

The business is also in violation of the PMC in regard to window signage. Pursuant to
PMC Section 17.88.070.M, the business may have one permanent non-illuminated
window sign not exceeding four square feet in area. Also, pursuant to PMC Section
17.88.070.N., the business may have temporary window signage not to exceed 25% of
the window area provided visiblity into the building is maintained. Temporary signage is
defined as a sign displayed for the specific period of time of an event, which is to be
removed immediately after the completion of the event or time period.

The business has been observed with window signage that covers a majority of the
windows. The signage exceeds 25% of the window area and limits visibilty into the
business. There are also iron bars for security on the inside of the business, which covers
a portion of the windows.

  B.  RESOLUTION

  NOW THEREFORE, it is hereby found, determined, and resolved by the Planning
  Commission of the City of Palmdale, as follows:

  1.  The Planning Commission hereby specifically finds that all of the facts set
  forth in the Recitals, Part A of this Resolution, are true and correct.

  2.  Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Commission during the
  above-referenced October 14, 2021, public hearing, including public
  testimony, and written and oral staff report, this Commission specifically
  finds as follows:

  (a)  The conditional use is not being conducted in compliance with the
  terms and conditions of the CUP and in an appropriate manner and
  that measures are not available to mitigate the impacts of the use.

  The Pro Cub Store business is in violation of Condition of Approval
  Nos. 17, 18, 19, 27 and 28, as well as the PMC as presented in the
  staff report dated October 14, 2021.

  The Pro Club Store is not being operated in an appropriate manner
  because it is not beneficial and desirous to the community and is
  adversely affecting adjacent property due to the crime and
  complaints associated with the business. Based on incident crime
  reports from the Los Angeles County Sherrif’s Department, Code
  Enforcement cases and pending legal proceedings, this business is
  a source of crime and is a nuisance to other properties in the vicinity.

  There are no available measures to mitigate the negative impacts of
  the business even with strict adherence to the Conditions of
  Approval, because the business is a known establishment for
  narcotics, gambling and other illicit activities as presented in the staff
  report dated October 14, 2021. Additionally, the applicant has a
  history of violating Conditions of Approval and the PMC, and new
  conditions imposed on the business will likely be ignored and
  therefore is not a viable solution to remediate or prevent the negative
  impacts of the business.

  Based on the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department incident
  crime reports, the Code Enforcement cases, the legal proceedings
  to abate the nuisance property, and the violation of the terms and
  conditions of the CUP, the business is not beneficial or desirous for
  the City of Palmdale and is not being operated in an appropriate
  manner.

  3.  Based on the findings and conclusions set forth in paragraphs 1 and 2
  above, this Commission hereby revokes CUP 17-016 without prejudice, and
  orders the business to cease and desist from using the subject property by
  November 15, 2021.

Plan Amendment (SPA) 18-003 and Tentative Tract Map (TTM) 61894 Major Modification

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The specific plan provides detailed, site-specific regulations, standards, and guidelines
for implementation of General Plan policies and priorities. The proposed project is a
request to amend the City Ranch (Anaverde) specific plan to reduce the overall number
of dwelling units, reduce the square footage of future commercial development, reduce
park acreage, allow for an active adult community, eliminate the golf course and modify
Conditions of Approval for TTM 61894. The Anaverde specific plan is situated on
approximately 1,400 acres generally located south of Elizabeth Lake Road between
Ranch Center Drive and Louise Lane (approximately 5,500 feet west of Tierra Subida
Avenue) and continuing south of Avenue S to the Palmdale City boundary (FIGURE 1).

  BACKGROUND

  On February 24, 1992, the City Ranch Specific Plan and EIR 89-03 were considered by
  the Planning Commission and recommended for approval by the City Council (General
  Plan Amendment 91-4, Pre-Zone 89-6, Specific Plan 89-3, and DA 92-2; RESOLUTION
  NOS. 92-13 and 91-114). The City Ranch Specific Plan and EIR were subsequently
  approved by the City Council (RESOLUTION 92-58 and Ordinance No. 971) in March of
  1992.

  DA 92-2 became effective on May 8, 1993, with an expiration date of May 10, 2013. On
  December 13, 2012, DA 92-2 was subsequently amended (Development Agreement
  Amendment 12-01) to modify timing and mitigation fees related to construction of the
  required fire station. On March 6, 2013, the City Council approved the amendment;
  however, the expiration date of the agreement was not amended, and the agreement
  expired on May 10, 2013.

  On March 14, 2005, the City Council approved TTM 61894 through RESOLUTION NO.
  CC 2005-060, which established an expiration date of May 10, 2013. Subsequently, two
  legislative time extensions (AB 333 and AB 208) were approved automatically extending
  the map for a total of four years until May 10, 2017. On July 11, 2017, the City Council
  approved RESOLUTION NO. CC 2017-030 for the first discretionary three-year time
  extension, which extended the expiration of the map until May 10, 2020. Subsequently,
  on September 28, 2020, an 18-month time extension pursuant to AB 1561 automatically
  extended the expiration of the map until November 10, 2021. On November 17, 2020, a
  second and final discretionary three-year time extension was approved by the City
  Council pursuant to RESOLUTION NO. CC 2020-102 extending the life of the map until
  November 10, 2024.

RECOMMENDATION

Adopt RESOLUTION NO. PC-2021-023, recommending City Council approval of Zoning
Ordinance Amendment (ZOA) 21-003 and find that the project is not subject to the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed ZOA would amend Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Chapters 17.16, 17.88
and 17.92 regarding signs, to ensure compliance with applicable laws, add clarifying
language, and modify standards to enhance flexibility for sign programs, sign types and
monument signs.

BACKGROUND

ZOA’s occur over time in order to improve the quality of life, provide convenience, and to
remain current with local government best practices. The PMC is currently out of
compliance with existing laws regarding signage and has internal inconsistences.
ZOA 21-003 addresses these issues by revising portions of the PMC to create a more
user-friendly document that is consistent with applicable laws and regulations and with
the General Plan. Failure to amend the code for conformance with State and Federal
regulations could lead to negative consequences for non-compliance.

  ANALYSIS

  The Amendment includes revisions that regulate signage by type, size, area, location,
  etc., rather than the content. In addition, the ZOA will provide language in order to ensure
  compliance with applicable laws and regulations and enhance flexibility for sign programs
  and monument signs. For example, the setback for monument signs will be reduced from
  ten feet to one foot from the public right-of-way. In addition, given that monument signs
  are proposed to be closer to the public right of way, provisions have been included
  requiring such signs to be installed in locations that ensure adequate site distance is
  maintained for both pedestrian and vehicular traffic. The Amendment also proposes
  greater flexibility for sign programs. Currently sign programs only allow a development
  to establish a cohesive design for signage with no deviations from the general
  development standards. The Amendment proposes to allow deviations in sign size,
  height, location design, etc. In addition, the Amendment proposes to allow one pole sign
  per development within the C-4 (Commercial Center) zone to ensure adequate signage
  is provided for development that offer goods and services to visiting and regional
  consumers.

  17.88.1540 Skyline Signs

  Skyline signs shall consist of wall signs that are placed on buildings of three stories or
  more. Signs on tall buildings can have a significant visual influence upon the community’s
  environment; therefore, they should be consistent with the architectural style of the
  building. The approval of skyline signs shall be subject to PMC 17.88.040, Sign Permits,
  and to the following standards:

  A.  Skyline Signs.

  1. Area. Signs shall be subject to the maximum sign area permitted for skyline
  signs within the zone as regulated under PMC 17.88.110 and 17.88.120.

  2.1. Placement. Skyline signs shall be placed
  above the vision glass windows of the highest
  floor of the building and below the eave line in
  accordance with the provisions for signs within the
  zone. In conventional high-rise design, a sizeable
  area is generally available for signs above the
  vision glass of the highest floor. Skyline signs
  shall not be located on any building elevation in
  vertical (stacked) alignment and shall be
  separated by a horizontal dimension of not less than forty (40) percent of the linear
  dimension of the subject elevation. For buildings with articulated roofs, a more
  flexible definition is appropriate. In such cases, signs are to be integrated visually
  with architectural features such as windows, projections and articulating elements.

  3.2. Proportion of sign area. To avoid the appearance of crowding a sign into a
  sign area, sign copy shall occupy no more than 80 percent of the horizontal skyline
  sign area as defined by this subsection. Additionally, no part of a sign can be located
  within the extreme left or right ten percent of the building elevation.

  4. Number of signs. Skyline signs shall be limited to one sign per allowable building
  elevation. Skyline signs shall only be placed on a maximum of two building
  elevations, which shall be opposite sides of the building.

  5. Skyline sign copy. Skyline signs shall consist of a single line of copy or symbols.
  However, subject to the review and approval of the Director of Planning, multiple
  lines of copy or symbols may be permitted where building architecture or the length
  of a sign prohibits a single line.

  6. Compatible materials. Skyline signs shall utilize material that is the same or
  appears to be the same or that is compatible with the building surfaces. Skyline

B.  Secondary skyline signs.

  1. Sign Area. Secondary skyline signs shall be subject to the maximum sign area
